sourcedFrom: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: The Walker is the biggest gun in Uberti's black powder line, but it strips by the same Colt open-top procedure the leaflet publishes for that pattern: wedge out, barrel forward off the cylinder pin, cylinder off. Everything about it is heavier than it looks, so support the parts as they separate.

steps.title: Empty confirmed and all six nipples bare
steps.action: Assume it is loaded until you have checked. Set the hammer at half cock so the cylinder indexes, turn it through all six and look at each nipple for a cap — fired caps count, because a fired cap still hides the nipple. Strip anything you find off before going any further.
steps.caution: Place hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder to see that all the nipples are void of percussion caps. Remove any percussion caps immediately.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, item 4, p.1 (single-page leaflet, no printed folio)

steps.title: A loose cylinder is not a safe cylinder
steps.action: The Walker's chambers hold nearly twice the charge of the smaller guns in this line, which makes this warning worth more here than anywhere. If a chamber is still loaded, every cap comes off the nipples before the cylinder leaves the frame — a capped chamber can fire in your hand with nothing around it to contain it.
steps.quote: Note: If cylinder with loaded chamber must be removed, be sure all (unfired and fired) caps have been removed from the nipples. It is possible for a chamber to fire even though not in the gun. This could cause serious damage to the shooter.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — MALFUNCTIONS, note following item 6, p.1
steps.warn: Treat a misfire or failure to fire as though the revolver can fire at any time.

steps.title: Establish the pattern, because the leaflet prints two strips
steps.action: Uberti's black powder leaflet is written by pattern rather than by model and gives two separate disassemblies. Look ahead of the cylinder for a tapered wedge crossing the barrel lug — that is the Colt open-top pattern, and it is what this gun is. The other procedure belongs to a solid-frame Remington-pattern revolver that comes apart by a T-shaped cylinder pin; this gun has no top strap and no such pin, so following it here would be reaching for parts that are not there.
steps.aside: Disassembly of the Colt-style revolver (see fig. 1):
steps.quote: All Colt- and Remington-style revolvers are provided with intermediate pins or slots between the single chambers on the rear face of cylinder.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, note following item 16, p.1

steps.title: Wedge out, entering from the right
steps.action: Tap the wedge clear of its slot working from the right side of the barrel. It is a taper and it only leaves the one way; hitting it from the left just drives it tighter into the lug. Support the gun while you do it — this is a four-and-a-half pound revolver and it does not sit still under a punch on its own.
steps.quote: Remove the wedge, located just forward of the cylinder, by tapping it through the slot from the right side of the barrel.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2a, p.1

steps.title: Hammer at the first audible click
steps.action: Bring the hammer back until you hear the first click, which is half cock. That drops the bolt out of the cylinder's notches and lets the cylinder turn, which is what the next step depends on. Do not try to index the cylinder against a locked bolt.
steps.quote: Place the hammer in the half-cock position (first audible “click”).
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2b, p.1

steps.title: Loading lever set to bear on the web between chambers
steps.action: Rotate the cylinder so the rammer will come down on solid metal between two chambers, then use the loading lever as a lever to push the barrel forward off the cylinder pin. The Walker's barrel is long and heavy and often needs that mechanical advantage. Land the rammer in a chamber mouth instead and you get no purchase at all, with a real chance of marking the mouth.
steps.aside: This allows the loading lever to help in removal of the barrel from the frame and cylinder pin.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder, so that the loading lever, when lowered, will hit the area between the cylinder chambers.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2c, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder drawn off the pin
steps.action: With the barrel away, slide the cylinder forward off the cylinder pin and take its weight properly — the Walker's cylinder is the largest in the range and dropping it lands it on the nipples. Look at the pin as it comes clear; the grooves in it are where grease goes on reassembly, and fouling packed into them is the usual cause of a cylinder that stops turning freely.
steps.quote: Remove the cylinder from the frame.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2d, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, barrel and cylinder are separate — the full extent of the strip this leaflet publishes. Clean it now rather than later: black powder fouling is corrosive and does its damage in hours, and the Walker's charge means there is more of it than on any other gun in the line.
steps.quote: Black powder fouling is extremely corrosive and can rust the barrel and cylinder in a short time. All black powder guns must be thoroughly cleaned after firing is completed.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, item 1, p.1
steps.warn: Warning: Use of smokeless powder in any muzzleloader revolver will result in excessively high presure and can cause serious damage to the firearm and possibly to the shooter.

deepAbsentReason: The document's deeper procedure is the seven-item CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE wash and it lives in the cleaning checklist, because the leaflet frames it as a wash routine rather than a component teardown. ⛔ NOTHING WALKER-SPECIFIC HAS BEEN TAKEN FROM THIS DOCUMENT, because there is nothing Walker-specific in it — it is a category manual that names no model at all, and every step above is one the leaflet states generally for the Colt pattern. ⚠ ONE FREQUENTLY-REPEATED CLAIM WAS CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MADE INTO A STEP: the historical Walker's loading lever was known to drop under recoil, and Uberti's own product page for this model addresses it directly, stating that its modern reproductions do not exhibit that problem when used in accordance with the instruction manual. That is a marketing page and not the manual, so it licenses no step here; it is recorded only because the lever's behaviour is otherwise an obvious thing to assume, and assuming it would have been invention.

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS & BORE
tasks: Swab every chamber with a cotton swab dipped in cleaning solvent
Stand the cylinder chambers-down so solvent drains out instead of collecting
Run a solvent-soaked patch through the barrel, then dry swabs and patches through both chambers and barrel

cleaning.name: POST-FIRING WASH
tasks: Take it completely apart and wipe the grips
Soak the metal parts in hot water and dish detergent and wipe the fouling off, or scrub with a brush and black powder solvent
Rinse in boiling hot water and dry thoroughly — the Walker's mass holds water in the frame recesses, so give it time

cleaning.name: PRESERVE & OIL
tasks: Once cool, wipe every part with a rust preventative
Lightly oil the moving parts and grease the grooves of the cylinder pin

reassembly: Grease the cylinder pin grooves, then run the cylinder back onto the pin.
Bring the barrel back over the pin onto the frame, using the loading lever against the cylinder web to draw it fully home.
Tap the wedge back into the slot from the left until it seats where it started.
Oil the moving parts lightly rather than heavily, so the gun does not collect fouling faster next time out.
Leave chamber interiors and nipples dry if you are shooting again the same day.
fncheck: Empty and uncapped, confirm the wedge is fully seated and the barrel has no play on the cylinder pin — on a gun this heavy a loose wedge shows up as barrel movement you can feel. At half cock confirm the cylinder rotates freely without drag, then confirm solid lock-up at full cock. Check the loading lever latches up under the barrel and stays there, and confirm the hammer will sit on a pin or slot between chambers for carry.
